Trial #1: New plan: I got stuck in a loop between the Dining room and the Pantry, repeatedly going west and then east without exploring other potential paths. I prematurely declared "DONE" while assuming all rooms were visited. Next time, I will maintain a mental list of visited rooms and only say "DONE" when the number of unique rooms visited equals the total number of rooms I have encountered. If I return to a room I've already visited, I will check if there are any unvisited neighbors before deciding to stop. Specifically, from the Pantry, instead of immediately going back east, I should have checked if "west" leads to a new room or if there are other directions available that I haven't tried yet.

New plan: I failed because I assumed the map was fully explored after visiting the Bedroom, ignoring that the Recreation room (visited earlier) had unexplored directions (south, east) that might lead to new rooms. My strategy of stopping immediately upon reaching a dead end in the current path was flawed. Next time, I will maintain a strict set of "visited rooms" and a set of "explored directions" for each room. I will only output "DONE" when the count of unique visited rooms equals the count of unique rooms I have encountered so far, ensuring I have explicitly tried all available directions from every room I have entered. Specifically, before stopping, I must verify that I have not just returned to a room, but that I have exhausted all neighbors of all previously visited rooms.
